title: cancel-in-progress means a run's own checkpoints cancel the CI its close-out waits for
description:
ci.yml declares:

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true

That is right for a human's feature branch, where a new push makes the old verdict irrelevant. It is wrong for an EPIC branch driven by a run, because the run pushes to that branch while its close-out waits for CI on it.

Observed closing Phase 4: the close-out held for CI on head 12c1aa0; checkpoint pushes moved the head to d2e0e5c and then 35f6e9f; each push cancelled the run in flight. Two consecutive CI runs were cancelled rather than completed, and gh reports a cancelled job as 'fail', so the close-out and the operator both read a cancellation as a red verdict.

This is 9da wearing a new coat. There the close-out could not find CI because the head kept moving; here it finds CI and the CI keeps being killed by the same movement. Both come from one fact: THE ACT OF GATING REWRITES THE THING BEING GATED.

Note it interacts badly with 9da's own fix. That fix walks back to an ancestor whose CI ran, proving nothing outside .ticfac/ changed. But if every ancestor's CI was CANCELLED rather than completed, there is no verdict anywhere to walk back to.

Options, none free:
- Exclude run-state-only pushes from triggering CI at all (paths-ignore on .ticfac/**), so a checkpoint neither starts nor cancels a run. Cheapest, and it matches the reasoning 9da already relies on: a .ticfac/ commit cannot change what the build compiles.
- Drop cancel-in-progress for epic/** refs only.
- Have the close-out treat 'cancelled' distinctly from 'failed' — necessary regardless, because they mean opposite things and today they are the same word.

The third is not optional. A cancelled check is not a red one, and reading it as red is how a green epic gets refused.

Found 2026-09-19 closing Phase 4.
notes:
2026-09-19 17:59 - 2026-09-19 — measured evidence, from the API rather than inference.

Commit 12c1aa0 on epic/ncv carries FOUR check runs:

    contracts: completed/success
    go:        completed/success
    sandbox:   completed/success
    typescript:completed/cancelled

forge.go's CI() maps 'cancelled' through its default branch to CIPending — deliberately, and the comment argues the case well: cancelled 'is not green, and saying the report is green would be the false close this seam exists to prevent'.

The consequence nobody intended: that commit is pending FOREVER. A cancelled check run is never replaced unless something re-runs on that exact commit, and 'gh run rerun --failed' on a later workflow does not touch it. So a commit superseded mid-flight by the run's own checkpoint push is permanently unusable as an ancestor verdict — which is precisely what 9da's walk needs ancestors for.

So the three failure modes now compound:
  - cancel-in-progress kills CI the run's own pushes supersede (this tick)
  - a cancelled run reads as pending, forever, on that commit
  - 9da's walk needs a CONCLUSIVE ancestor, and these commits never become one

Confirmed healthy by contrast: 35f6e9f, re-run to completion, carries 4x completed/success and nothing else, and everything between it and the head touches only .ticfac/. That is the shape the walk is built for, so the walk itself is sound — it is being starved of conclusive ancestors rather than failing at its job.

Suggests the cheapest fix is even more clearly paths-ignore on .ticfac/**: a checkpoint that never starts a workflow also never cancels one, and never leaves a permanently-pending commit behind.
acceptance_criteria: A run's checkpoint pushes neither cancel nor falsely fail the CI its close-out gates on, and a cancelled check is never reported as a failing one
